summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 99) follows Lee-Daniel, a company founder, during a tense moment at CogRad as a network message is relayed through staff. Lee-Daniel weighs whether to stay on after his company's leadership transition, while the investors watch. Mac, the company's executive, pressures him to remain, flattering him and promising a large payout and an IPO, though Lee-Daniel suspects Mac is just massaging his ego.
one_line: Lee-Daniel, ousted from his company CogRad, is pressed by Mac to stay on through the leadership transition in exchange for a big IPO payday.
key_facts: Lee-Daniel asks Mac about the critical path between tonight and the arrival of an executive search for a new CEO.
Lee-Daniel hired the switchgirl, a network engineer, from a backwater DeVry at a job fair in Tulsa.
The switchgirl ran a little to fat but was still broad-shouldered from using a rowing machine she carried from gig to gig.
Mortimer boomed into the auditorium mic asking "You want something, boss?"
Mac tells Lee-Daniel, "We thought you'd stay on, LD, help with a smooth transition."
Mac says the company does not want to dismantle CogRad but wants to grow it into something big and important.
Lee-Daniel suspects Mac is blowing smoke and massaging his ego.
Mac claims he fought hard to keep Lee-Daniel in place during the transition.
Mac says Lee-Daniel is the only one who can train his successor.
Mac predicts Lee-Daniel could retire on his share in 18 months if the plan goes as expected.
Mac plans to franchise the company, start new busses, and turn it into a turnkey solution that scales.
Mac says the company will raise 10 billion on IPO if it raises a cent.
The Series A and Series B investors watch the exchange silently like a tennis match.
Mac sends the investors away to get beers, and they leave petulantly.
